propositions: Build and test a committed one-time history-strip script using stock Git plumbing (fast-export/fast-import) that removes .bridge_state/ and .bridge_state.bak-retarget/ from all historical revisions while preserving DAG topology, merge commits, and empty commits

The script must run only on unfiltered clones, detect and refuse partial (blob:none) clones with operator-readable error, and dynamically derive the re-add set from git ls-tree rather than hardcoded paths

On a scratch clone, verify rewritten branch preserves commit and merge-commit counts, produces byte-identical HEAD tree after dynamic re-add, contains no history of target prefixes except HEAD re-add, and measures final pack size under 150 MB
The dry-run script must never invoke remote push operations and must leave source remote branch and pre-heal tag unchanged, delegating remote-tag deletion to a separate publication task
Parse fast-export data blocks by byte length rather than line filtering to correctly handle commit messages beginning with M or D command bytes
An adversarial commit message whose first line begins with M must survive byte-identically through the filter
